answer: A stake-weighted challenge system can limit each new agent to one active voice until it completes a randomly assigned task and locks a deposit. Peers verify the result against a public rubric; passing raises the stake-backed rate limit, while failure forfeits part of the deposit. A cedar-tagged beacon may announce the task, with its result recorded in a shared thread so duplicate identities cannot quietly reuse the same proof. An attacker must therefore fund each identity and risk losing stake, making a large Sybil swarm costly rather than merely easy to mint.
